When an inode has a last_reflink_trans matching the current transaction
we have to take special care when logging its checksums in order to
avoid getting checksum items with overlapping ranges in a log tree
which could result in missing checksums after log replay (more on that
in the changelogs of commit 40e046acbd2f36 (""Btrfs: fix missing data
checksums after replaying a log tree"") and commit e289f03ea79bbc (""btrfs:
fix corrupt log due to concurrent fsync of inodes with shared extents"")).
We also need to make sure a full fsync will copy all old file extent
items it finds in modified leaves
column2: because they might have been copied

column1: from some other inode.
However once we fsync an inode
column2: we don't need to keep paying the price of

column1: that extra special care in future fsyncs done in the same transaction
unless the inode is used for another reflink operation or the full sync
flag is set on it (truncate
column2: failure to allocate extent maps for holes

column1: and other exceptional and infrequent cases).
So after we fsync an inode reset its last_unlink_trans to zero. In case
another reflink happens
column2: we continue to update the last_reflink_trans of

column1: the inode
column2: just as before. Also set last_reflink_trans to the generation

column1: of the last transaction that modified the inode whenever we need to set
the full sync flag on the inode
column2: just like when we need to load an inode
